name: OpenMoji
author: the OpenMoji project (HfG Schwaebisch Gmuend and contributors)

data.what: the release's table of every emoji (4,495 entries): emoji, hexcode, group, subgroups, annotation (its name), tags (Unicode CLDR keywords), openmoji_tags, openmoji_author, openmoji_date, skin tone fields, unicode, order. Not kept here (2.2 MB); openmoji-names.json is made from it.

LICENSE.txt.what: the full text of the license, from the repository at tag 17.0.0, unchanged (the same legal code as data/vendor/mulberry/CC-BY-SA-4.0.txt but for three blank lines)

table.what: made by dev-tools/build_word_sounds_symbols.cjs --openmoji-from from data/openmoji.json (sha256 above): only the emoji named with one word and without a skin tone, and only hexcode, annotation, group, subgroups, unicode, tags, openmoji_tags and openmoji_author

symbols.what: The emoji files a Word Sounds word could use, and no others: every OpenMoji candidate of every matched word in data/word_sounds_symbols_map_en.json (used or held for review). Each file is the release's color SVG <hexcode>.svg, unchanged, byte for byte.
symbols.digest: sha256 of the lines "<sha256 of the file>  <file name>\n", sorted by file name (dev-tools/build_word_sounds_symbols.cjs, symbolsDigest)

matching: OpenMoji is the second set: a word gets an OpenMoji picture only when no Mulberry symbol has its name (or its singular's), only by the emoji's own name (annotation): the emoji named exactly the word, or the word is the plain plural of that name and the emoji shows a thing. One emoji of the name: used ("auto"). Several: the one in Unicode is used when only one is, else a person chooses. The keywords (tags) are never used to match: they are loose (the pig is tagged "bacon", the yin yang "difficult", the oncoming fist "absolutely"). Where Mulberry holds a word for a person, OpenMoji's emoji of that name is added to the choices, never used on its own.
exclusions: Never used, whatever the word (dev-tools/build_word_sounds_symbols.cjs: OPENMOJI_EXCLUDED_SUBGROUPS, OPENMOJI_EXCLUDED_TAGS, OPENMOJI_NOT_THE_WORD, OPENMOJI_ALLOWED; the review sheet lists them and every emoji they leave out): (1) flags of any kind and flag letters, unless the word is "flag"; (2) skin tones and hair parts, and every skin-tone variant (only the base emoji is in the table); (3) company logos; (4) screen and app icons, letters, numbers and keycaps, gender signs; (5) religious symbols and buildings, astrology signs, and anything whose keywords name a religion or a religious holiday (Christmas, Easter, Hanukkah, Diwali, Ramadan...); (6) flags and symbols of movements and causes, and anything whose keywords name politics, protest, voting or elections; (7) hand gestures (some are rude), other gestures, couples and kisses, except the handshake; (8) fantasy figures and costume faces (some are frightening or religious), except fairy, mermaid, merman, merperson, superhero, robot and alien; cursing, devil and skull faces; signs for a feeling that do not show the word; (9) medicines, needles, blood and medical scenes, emergency signs; (10) anything whose keywords name alcohol, tobacco or drugs (pills; not "medicine", which also tags the hospital), weapons (including the axe, bow and arrow, knife and sword), violence, death, crime, war, frightening things, romance or underwear, gambling, or rude things; (11) an emoji that is another word spelled the same (mate is the drink, led is a lamp, pick is a pickaxe) or a picture a child would not read as the word (lighter, wedding chapel, town (its drawing has a church with a cross), dizzy symbol, tablet, and the electronics symbols switch, motor, cable, wire, drone). Gendered variants: an emoji that is the man or woman form of another is used only when its own name is the word (mermaid, prince, princess); matching by exact name never picks one for a word that has no gender.
changes: The vendored files are unchanged. The page data (word_sounds_symbols/en-<n>.json, with its index word_sounds_symbols_en.js) holds, as text, the drawings of the used words that have a recording, OpenMoji drawings in their own data file. The script passes each through a tidy-up that removes only the space between tags and at the ends (the OpenMoji files are indented); no drawing is redrawn, recolored, cropped or turned into pixels.
remake: Download the zip (url above) and data/openmoji.json at the tag (data.url), check both sha256, unzip the zip into a folder beside openmoji.json (or into its subfolder x), then: node dev-tools/build_word_sounds_symbols.cjs --openmoji-from <that folder>. That remakes openmoji-names.json, copies the emoji files that are needed, updates "symbols" and "table" here, and re-makes the map, the index and the data files. Without it the script works from what is vendored here; --check fails when anything is out of date. The zip (5.4 MB) and the full table are not kept in the repo.
scope: Pictures for single words in Word Sounds practice packets, when the teacher checks "Include pictures", for words Mulberry Symbols has no picture for. A packet embeds only the pictures of its own words, credits each set it uses under About this file, and carries each set's license notice in its manifest.
shareAlike: The emoji stay a separately licensed work: they live in this folder and in their own data file in word_sounds_symbols/ under CC BY-SA 4.0, apart from the AGPL-3.0 program, and that data file says so in its first line. A packet with OpenMoji pictures is a collection of the program and the pictures; the pictures in it stay under CC BY-SA 4.0. Anyone who changes a drawing must share the changed drawing under the same license.
limitations: OpenMoji is an emoji set: its pictures are small icons drawn for screens, mostly things, animals, food, places and people; it has few actions and no describing words. Matching is by the emoji's English name, written for emoji users, not for children learning to read: a name can be another word spelled the same (the exclusions list the ones found). The script author checked the exclusions against every emoji named like a usable word (2026-11-12) and looked at every used picture once; a reviewer has not yet looked at the used pictures (see the review sheet the script writes).
